newsitem.title: USA: CME Oct live cattle end up on rising beef prices.
newsitem.headline: CME Oct live cattle end up on rising beef prices.

text.p: Sharp advances so far this week in wholesale beef values to 11-month highs bolstered October CME live cattle futures late despite profit taking after that contract posted a new contract high early, traders said.
Feeder cattle futures set new highs but slipped to close mostly lower when corn futures rebounded from early declines.

October live cattle set a new high of 73.950 cents per lb early but slowly eased on profit taking to close 0.300 higher at 73.625 cents. Other live cattle months ended 0.075 cent lower to 0.200 higher.
Rolling of short positions added to demand from higher beef prices to support October while pressing December.
Soaring boxed beef values Monday sparked commercial demand early and short covering continued, especially following another surge in beef values at noon.

Heavyweight choice beef prices have jumped $4.89 per cwt to $109.72, the highest level since November 3, 1995, in the past two days, which encouraged ideas that packers' margins were better which would in turn, prompt them to raise bids fed cattle, traders said.
"Packers cut back the slaughter and this boosted the beef prices," one trader said of recent slaughter operations.

R.J. O'Brien, Rand Financials, Refco and RBH notably bought early with buy stops adding to the advance. Various houses bought October and sold December and Lind-Waldock notably spread long February/short December. Stone Traders bought April/and sold February, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, E.D.& F. Man bought February 70 and 72 calls. Lit bought April 66 puts and sold 60 puts, pit sources added.
November feeder cattle posted a new contract high of 66.050 cents a lb and January 66.100 cents early with distant May through September also setting new contract highs before slipping.
Feeders closed 0.075 cent higher to 0.200 lower with October ending off 0.050 at 64.400 cents.
Lower corn futures, the rally in live cattle and higher CME feeder index supported feeders early, traders said. But prices retreated for net losses as corn futures rose, they said.
Locals sold October which offset buying by ING, traders said, while Prudential and ING sold November. Cargill and Stone Traders spread long October/short February live cattle early, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index rose $0.30 to $63.60 per cwt.
